g.text: Nonconformity management — from entry to closure
(reported by an internal or external party)
Analysis, actions and follow-ups: the app
enforces no order. Their “+” buttons stay
available as long as the NC is neither
Enter the analysis: root cause, 5 Whys
NC “CAPA defined” on the first action
Carry out the action, enter the completion date
Plan the follow-up: criterion, date, linked actions
Upload the file to the evidence library
once any evidence exists, direct or via a linked action
Verify effectiveness, enter the verification date
the NC returns to “CAPA in progress”
No version can be created on a “Closed” NC.
Write or carry over the three summaries:
Generate the draft PDF for review (optional)
No check on the NC status:
Regenerate the PDF marked “Version n — FOR SIGNATURE”
record locked: fields read-only, “+” buttons hidden
Send the PDF to the approver
Review the report, then sign or refuse it
Submit the signed PDF and its signature date,
on or after the version date
Store the file, then set the version to “Signed”
(refusal, or revision of a signed report)
Close the NC, with a closure date
on or after the signature date
Closure is a human act: the app sees that
a file is present, not that it is signed.
Evidence can still be added to the record,
but no longer removed or modified.
Status set or recalculated by the app, with no data entry
Power Automate flow called by the app
Decision: “App:” = automatic test, otherwise human decision
Statuses follow from the recorded facts; judgments
(approve, reject, sign, close) remain human acts.
